election_dates.primarySnippet: MCL 168.52: A general primary election of all political parties shall be held in every election precinct in this state on the Tuesday succeeding the first Monday in August preceding every general November election in which a governor is to be elected, at which time the qualified and registered electors of each political party shall vote for party candidates for the office of governor.
election_dates.generalSnippet: MCL 168.641: The November regular election date, which is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.

state_background_check.value: No — Michigan's constitutional felony bar applies only to state and local elective office and public employment by its own text (not federal office), and even there only reaches a felony involving dishonesty, deceit, fraud, or breach of public trust committed in the person's official capacity within the preceding 20 years; separately, the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state, so this doesn't reach U.S. House or Senate candidates either way
state_background_check.snippet: Mich. Const. art. XI, § 8: "A person is ineligible for election or appointment to any state or local elective office of this state and ineligible to hold a position in public employment in this state that is policy-making or that has discretionary authority over public assets if, within the immediately preceding 20 years, the person was convicted of a felony involving dishonesty, deceit, fraud, or a breach of the public trust and the conviction was related to the person's official capacity while the person was holding any elective office or position of employment in local, state, or federal government." Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

primary_results.snippet: Donavan McKinney, Taras Nykoriak, Christopher Dardzinski, Simone Coleman, Shelby Campbell, and Maurice Morton are running in the general election for U.S. House Michigan District 13 on November 3, 2026. Open seat: incumbent Shri Thanedar lost the Democratic primary to McKinney by about 4 points. Coleman has no FEC 2026 registration found; Campbell's only FEC matches (Democratic Party, not Independent as Ballotpedia lists her) don't confidently identify the same person, so she's excluded rather than force an uncertain match; see code comment.

platform.value: Supports Medicare for All, which would ensure everyone in this country has healthcare including coverage for dental, vision, mental health, reproductive health and abortion care, and community-based long term support services.
platform.snippet: As a former leader within SEIU Healthcare Michigan, I know our families cannot afford anything less than Medicare for All, which would ensure everyone in this country has healthcare — no matter their employment status, zip code, race, gender, sexuality, or disability. Medicare for All would include coverage for dental, vision, mental health, reproductive health and abortion care. It would also include community-based long term support services, ensuring hundreds of thousands of disabled people are able to finally get the home care they need.

platform.value: Committed to transforming the criminal justice system including ending cash bail, reallocating funding to invest in social, health, and rehab services, reforming sentencing guidelines, ending the school-to-prison pipeline, and ending qualified immunity.
platform.snippet: I am committed to doing all that I can in Congress to transform the criminal justice system. That includes ending cash bail, because we should not be jailing people simply because they are poor. It includes reallocating funding to invest in social, health, and rehab services so that we are able to reach people who are at risk of incarceration before they end up stuck in the system. It also includes reforming sentencing guidelines, ending the school-to-prison pipeline by investing in quality public education and wrap-around services for all our youth, ending qualified immunity, and much more.

bio_summary.value: Donavan McKinney is a lifelong Detroiter, proud husband, and devoted father. He grew up in northeast Detroit, and was raised by his mother and grandmother, where poverty wages led to many evictions and forced his family to move over 13 times. A proud product of Detroit Public Schools and the first in the family to graduate from college (Go Blue!), Donavan worked as a leader of SEIU Healthcare Michigan and currently serves as State Representative where he is delivering tangible results for everyday people.

bio_summary.value: Born of Detroit's grit and raised on its work ethic: a fighter for the 13th District who answers to the people who live here, not to a party or a donor class. He has stood in the places most candidates only talk about. He traveled to Ukraine in 2022 and 2023, where he saw firsthand how American resources can go unaccounted for, and came home determined that Congress ask the hard questions. His campaign is built on the oath itself: defend the Constitution, protect the rights of every citizen, and treat public office as a public trust rather than a career.
